title: Integral geometry of marked nodal curves after a birational base change
statement: Let $F$ be a field [def-weil-field], $S$ an integral finite-type $F$-scheme, and $f:T\to S$ a projective morphism in the projective-bundle convention, flat and finitely presented [def-pc-integral-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-trf-projective-bundle-morphism, def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Assume its geometric fibres are nonempty connected reduced one-dimensional nodal curves [def-trf-nodal-geometric-fibres], and its generic fibre is smooth and geometrically integral [def-weil-geometric-fibre, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]. Let $D\subset S$ be closed, assume $f$ smooth over $S\setminus D$, and let $M\hookrightarrow T$ be a finite disjoint union of sections in the relative smooth locus [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Let $t:S_0\to S$ be a projective birational surjection in the same convention with $S_0$ integral and smooth over $F$. Birational means an isomorphism between dense opens with equal function fields. Put $W=T\times_SS_0$, $g:W\to S_0$, $q:W\to T$, $M_0=M\times_SS_0$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Then $S,S_0,T,W$ are Noetherian finite-type $F$-schemes, $T$ and $W$ are integral, and both $g$ and $q$ are projective in the projective-bundle convention and proper [def-weil-proper-morphism]. The morphism $g$ is flat and finitely presented with the same stated geometric fibre properties, smooth over $S_0\setminus t^{-1}D$, with smooth geometrically integral generic fibre. The marking $M_0$ is again a finite disjoint union of sections in its smooth locus. Inverse images of dense base opens under $f$ and $g$ are dense, and $q$ is birational and surjective. If a finite group $J$ acts compatibly on $F,S,T,S_0$, makes $f,t$ equivariant and preserves $D,M$, its diagonal action on $W$ makes $g,q$ equivariant and preserves $M_0$ and $|M_0|\cup g^{-1}(t^{-1}D)$. Actions on $F$ may be nontrivial. Empty $D$ and $M$ are allowed. Noetherian means locally Noetherian and quasi-compact [pqf-def-locnoeth].

proof.text: Apply projective-bundle base change first to $f$ along $t$, and then to $t$ along $f$; these give respectively $g$ and $q$ projective in the required convention. Projective-bundle properness gives properness of $f,t,g,q$, hence finite type of each. A field has only the ideals $(0)$ and $(1)$, so $\operatorname{Spec}F$ is Noetherian. Finite-type composition makes $T,W$ finite type over $F$; $S$ is so by hypothesis and $S_0$ by finite-type composition with $t$. Finite type over a Noetherian scheme now gives Noetherianity of all four schemes.

Flat base change makes $g$ flat; finite-presentation base change makes it finitely presented. For every algebraically closed $\Omega$ and $z:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to S_0$, the fibre-product universal property identifies $W_z$ with $T_{tz}$ over $\Omega$. Thus nonemptiness, connectedness, reducedness, dimension one and the completed nodal local-ring condition are exactly the assumed properties of $T_{tz}$. This uses geometric tests over arbitrary algebraically closed fields, as specified in the nodal-fibre definition, rather than identifying unrelated algebraic closures.

proof.text: The given dense-open isomorphism for $t$ identifies the generic points and their local rings, hence their residue fields. Write the common field as $K$. Fibre-product associativity identifies $W_{\eta_0}$ with $T_\eta$ over this identification of fields. Consequently the generic fibre of $g$ is smooth and geometrically integral. The morphism $g$ over $S_0\setminus t^{-1}D$ is the base change of $f$ over $S\setminus D$, so smoothness follows from smooth base change.

source.place: Tag 01VB (lemma-base-change-smooth); ILO X Lemma 2.2 proof, p.149, base modification; generic-field identification is the given dense-open isomorphism.

proof.text: For either $h=f$ or $h=g$, its flatness and local finite presentation make $h$ open. Every nonempty source open $O$ therefore has nonempty open image in its integral base; that image contains the generic point. Thus $O$ meets the generic fibre, whose image is dense. More generally, for every dense base open $V$, the nonempty open $h(O)$ meets $V$, so $O$ meets $h^{-1}V$. This proves exactly the asserted density of inverse images of dense opens.

source.place: Tag 01UA (flat locally finitely presented morphisms are universally open); density argument written here.

proof.text: For $h=f$ or $g$, take a nonempty affine source open $\operatorname{Spec}B$ mapping into an affine base open $\operatorname{Spec}A$. The ring $A$ is a domain; the affine flatness criterion and flat torsion-freeness show $B\to B\otimes_A\operatorname{Frac}(A)$ injective: a numerator killed in this localization is killed by some nonzero element of $A$. The mutually inverse fraction maps $b\otimes(a/s)\mapsto ab/s$ and $b/s\mapsto b\otimes(1/s)$ identify the tensor product with this localization. The affine-fibre tensor formula and affine fibre-product lemma identify its spectrum with the induced affine open of the integral generic fibre. That open is nonempty by Step 4, so its ring is a domain. Hence $B$ is a domain. These affine source opens cover the total space, which is therefore reduced.

source.place: Tag 01U5 (lemma-flat-characterize); schemes.tex Tag 01I4 (lemma-fibre-product-affine-schemes); torsion-free localization calculation written here.

proof.text: For either total space, any two nonempty opens have nonempty inverse images in its generic fibre by Step 4. Those inverse images intersect because the generic fibre is integral. Their intersection maps into the intersection of the original opens. The total space is therefore irreducible, is nonempty because its generic fibre is, and is reduced by Step 5. The reduced-and-irreducible characterization of integrality gives $T$ and $W$ integral.

The proper birational generic-isomorphism-open lemma applies to $t$: $S$ is Noetherian by Step 1, $t$ is proper, and its generic local-ring map is the field isomorphism in Step 3. Obtain a dense open $V\subset S$ with $t^{-1}V\to V$ an isomorphism. Base change gives an isomorphism $q^{-1}(f^{-1}V)\to f^{-1}V$. Both opens are dense by Step 4, so $q$ is birational; on this common dense open its generic stalk map is the identity under the induced identification, giving equality of function fields. Surjectivity of $q$ is surjective base change applied to the assumed surjectivity of $t$.

For each marked section $s:S\to T$, define $s_0:S_0\to W$ by the pair $(s\circ t,\mathrm{id}_{S_0})$. The fibre-product equations give $g\circ s_0=\mathrm{id}_{S_0}$. Its image subscheme is the base change of the image of $s$, so is closed by closed-immersion base change. The base changes of two disjoint marked components remain disjoint, since their intersection is the pullback of their empty intersection; their finite union is $M_0$. Around each original marked point choose an open on which $f$ is smooth; smooth base change supplies a smooth open around each pulled-back marking. This also proves the empty-marking case.

source.place: Tags 01QR (lemma-base-change-closed-immersion), 01VB (lemma-base-change-smooth); section equations by the fibre-product universal property.

proof.text: For $j\in J$, define $a_j:W\to W$ by $q a_j=j_Tq$ and $g a_j=j_{S_0}g$. The two components have equal composites to $S$ because $f,t$ are equivariant. The fibre-product universal property gives $a_1=\mathrm{id}$ and $a_j a_k=a_{jk}$, and $a_{j^{-1}}$ is the inverse. This construction is in schemes, so nontrivial field automorphisms cause no difficulty. The equations make $q,g$ equivariant. Since $M_0$ is the pullback of $M$ its image is preserved. Since $t^{-1}D$ is invariant, $g^{-1}(t^{-1}D)$ is invariant as well, hence so is their union. The same equations apply when either marking or boundary is empty.

Steps 1-9 are all correct. Step 1 gets projectivity of g and q from the new lemma along t and along f, properness from projective-bundle properness, and Noetherianity from finite type over Spec F. Step 2 transfers every nodal-fibre property because the definition tests every algebraically closed Ω. Step 5 shows the total space is integral: B is flat hence torsion-free over the domain A, so B injects into B⊗Frac A, the ring of a nonempty affine open of the integral generic fibre. Step 7 gets birationality of q from lem-sfb-birational-generic-isomorphism-open, using that S is Noetherian (Step 1), plus density from Step 4. Step 8 builds the sections as s_0=(st,id). Step 9 builds the diagonal action from universal-property uniqueness. I checked the source ILO X Lemma 2.2 (printed p.149-150): it gives no proof of this geometry, so proof_origin agent is right.
